questions.scenario: Your friends are planning a trip to a local cafe and a movie. Everyone hands over their cash to you. What is your very first instinct?

options.A: I physically count the cash twice, keep it safely in my wallet, and hold onto the physical movie tickets.
options.B: I double-check the final cafe bill to make sure the waiter didn't accidentally add items we never ordered.
options.C: I suggest a combo-offer or a discount code so we can save enough to buy popcorn during the interval.
options.D: I take charge, set the maximum budget for the outing, and decide which cafe fits our overall limit.

questions.scenario: It's the end of the month and you are checking your 'gullak' (piggy bank) or pocket money savings. How do you handle it?

options.A: I empty the gullak, physically stack the 10 and 20 rupee coins in piles, and count them one by one to ensure nothing is missing.
options.B: I mentally calculate where every single rupee went this month and investigate why I have 50 rupees less than I expected.
options.C: I mentally divide my savings into 'snack fund', 'gaming fund', and 'savings for a new phone cover'.
options.D: I prepare a solid pitch about my 'increased expenses and good grades' to negotiate a pocket money increment from my parents.

questions.scenario: You are out for Diwali shopping with your family in a crowded market. What is your role?

options.A: I hold the physical shopping bags and actively check off items from Mummy's handwritten list as we buy them.
options.B: I quickly compare prices online on my phone to catch if the local shopkeeper is giving us a fake 'festival discount'.
options.C: I convince my parents to buy a bulk pack of sweets so we save enough money to buy extra fairy lights and diyas.
options.D: I remind everyone of the total shopping budget before we leave the house and stop my sibling from overspending on useless crackers.

questions.scenario: Your colony is organizing a huge Ganesh Chaturthi or Navratri pandal. How do you help out the committee?

options.A: I walk door-to-door in the society to collect the 'chanda' (donation) and write out the physical receipts on the spot.
options.B: I closely scrutinize the tent-wala's and decorator's final bills to find any hidden charges or double billing.
options.C: I figure out how to stretch the collected funds so we can afford a better DJ without cutting the prasad budget.
options.D: I take the lead in the youth committee, approving major expenses and overseeing the entire event's execution.

questions.scenario: Mummy has set some very strict rules about screen time and studying. How do you navigate this?

options.A: I follow the rules perfectly and keep a close eye on my siblings to make sure they aren't breaking them either.
options.B: I find a logical loophole. 'You said no watching TV, you never said I couldn't play games on the iPad!'
options.C: I negotiate a win-win deal: 'If I study for 2 hours straight now, can I get 1 hour of extra gaming time on Sunday?'
options.D: I sit her down and make a strong, big-picture case for why my curfew and screen time should be permanently extended.

questions.scenario: You and your friends are eating at a local street food stall (Golgappas/Momos). What are you doing?

options.A: I stand right next to the bhaiya, physically counting exactly how many puris he gives to each person in our circle.
options.B: I notice immediately when he accidentally charges us for an extra plate of momos and point out the math error.
options.C: I suggest we order a large family platter instead of individual plates because it's way more cost-effective for the group.
options.D: I declare myself the host, treat everyone, and decide which stall we go to next based on quality and crowd.

questions.scenario: It is your best friend's birthday and your group is throwing a surprise party. What is your primary task?

options.A: I go to the bakery, verify the cake design myself, and carefully transport it on my scooty/cycle to the venue.
options.B: I keep a sharp eye on the WhatsApp group, making sure no one conveniently 'forgot' to GPay their share of the party.
options.C: I come up with creative, low-cost DIY decoration ideas so we have more money left to buy a really cool gift.
options.D: I assign roles to everyone (who distracts the friend, who buys the balloons) and oversee the entire mission.

questions.scenario: There is only one packet of Maggi left and both you and your sibling want it. How is this resolved?

options.A: I physically divide the cooked Maggi into two bowls, measuring them side-by-side so they are exactly equal down to the last noodle.
options.B: I interrogate my sibling to find out if they secretly have another stash of snacks hidden in their cupboard.
options.C: I trade my least favorite chocolates for their half of the Maggi, executing a perfect snack-swap strategy.
options.D: I declare myself the owner of the kitchen for the evening and set the rules on who gets to eat what and when.

questions.scenario: Your group is assigned a major school project that requires a lot of chart paper, files, and craft work. What is your role?

options.A: I volunteer to go to the local stationery shop, buy the chart papers, and check everything off our physical supply list.
options.B: I proofread the final project file, spotting tiny spelling mistakes or factual errors that everyone else completely missed.
options.C: I figure out how we can use old magazines and leftover craft materials from home so we don't have to spend our pocket money.
options.D: I act as the group leader, delegating tasks to each member and ensuring the project is ready before the submission deadline.

questions.scenario: The TV remote (or house keys) is lost again. Total chaos! What is your approach to finding it?

options.A: I physically flip every sofa cushion, look under the beds, and inspect every corner of the drawing room.
options.B: I logically retrace everyone's steps, cross-questioning my family members until I deduce who had it last.
options.C: I devise a plan to assign a specific permanent tray for the remotes and keys so we never face this issue again.
options.D: I declare a 'search party' and offer a small reward (like a chocolate) to whichever sibling finds it first.

Field_Auditor.title: Field Auditor / Inspector
Field_Auditor.primary_match_text: The Action-Oriented Verifier! You love being in the thick of it, physically checking things, and making sure everything matches up perfectly.
Field_Auditor.day_in_the_life: Traveling to different client sites, walking through massive warehouses, counting physical inventory, and cross-checking bills to ensure no stock or money is missing.
Field_Auditor.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th Commerce -> B.Com/BBA -> CA Foundation -> CA Intermediate -> 3 Years Articleship (focus on Statutory/Internal Audit) -> CA Final.

Forensic_Accountant.title: Forensic Accountant / Tax Analyst
Forensic_Accountant.primary_match_text: The Financial Detective! You have an eagle eye for details, loopholes, and errors. Nothing escapes your logical scrutiny.
Forensic_Accountant.day_in_the_life: Diving deep into complex bank statements, finding hidden money, exposing financial frauds, and solving corporate tax mysteries like a real-life detective.
Forensic_Accountant.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th Commerce -> B.Com -> CA Foundation & Inter -> Articleship (focus on Forensic Audit or Taxation) -> CA Final -> Certificate Course on Forensic Accounting & Fraud Detection (FAFD).

Financial_Planner.title: Financial Planner / Wealth Advisor
Financial_Planner.primary_match_text: The Strategy Architect! You love making resources stretch, planning for the future, and giving people clever advice to maximize their gains.
Financial_Planner.day_in_the_life: Meeting clients, understanding their life goals (like buying a house or funding their child's education), and designing personalized investment portfolios to grow their wealth.
Financial_Planner.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th Commerce -> BBA/B.Com -> Certified Financial Planner (CFP) OR Chartered Accountancy (CA) / Cost and Management Accountancy (CMA) -> Specialization in Wealth Management.

Chief_Financial_Officer.title: Chief Financial Officer (CFO) / Firm Partner
Chief_Financial_Officer.primary_match_text: The Big-Picture Boss! You are a natural leader who thinks about the overall budget, strategy, and makes the heavy-hitting decisions.
Chief_Financial_Officer.day_in_the_life: Sitting in the boardroom, managing a multi-crore company budget, leading a massive team of accountants, and deciding exactly where the company should invest its profits next.
Chief_Financial_Officer.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th Commerce -> B.Com/BBA -> CA / CMA / Company Secretary (CS) -> Optional MBA in Finance from a top B-School (like IIMs) -> Years of corporate leadership experience.
